draft.title: Superannuation and the Age Pension
card: The Age Pension is a regular payment from the Australian Government to older people who need support. It is paid for from taxes.
People with more super have more of their own income in retirement. This lets them live better than the Age Pension alone would allow. Fewer of them need the full pension.
Australia's population is ageing. More people are retiring and fewer workers pay tax for each retiree, which pushes up the total cost of the Age Pension.
If more retirees can fund themselves with super, the cost of the Age Pension to government is eased.
draft.remember: More super means fewer retirees rely on the full Age Pension, easing its cost to government.

a.q: Across the population, what happens to the Age Pension when more people build up higher super savings?
opts: Fewer people need the full pension, which eases the cost
More people need the full pension, which raises the cost
The pension is no longer paid to anyone at all
The pension costs more because retirees spend less
a.why: When retirees have more super, fewer need the full Age Pension, so the cost to government is eased. The pension does not stop being paid, because some people still need support.
a.clue: Think about who needs government support if they have their own savings.

b.q: Why does Australia's ageing population make super matter more for government budgets?
opts: Pension costs rise while fewer workers pay tax per retiree
Pension costs fall while more workers pay tax per retiree
Retirees need less super because they live longer lives
Pension costs fall because fewer people reach retirement age
b.why: As more people retire and fewer workers pay tax for each retiree, the total cost of the Age Pension goes up. Super helps because retirees who fund themselves need less from the pension. The option with more workers per retiree reverses what ageing does.
b.clue: Compare the number of retirees with the workers who pay tax.
